name: Mount Toubkal Circuit Trek
summary: A loop out of Imlil through Tacheddirt, Amsouzert and Lake Ifni, crossing Tizi Likemt (3,555 m), Tizi n'Ououraine (3,120 m) and Tizi n'Ouanoums (3,664 m) before the Neltner hut. Most itineraries finish with the ascent of Toubkal itself, which is the high point of the route at 4,167 m.

name: High Atlas Trek
summary: An umbrella name rather than a single route: operators sell village-to-village crossings of the High Atlas lasting anywhere from six days to three weeks, some finishing on Toubkal, some on M'Goun, some on neither. Duration, high point and grade depend entirely on which itinerary is booked, so they are not stated here.

name: M'Goun Massif Trek
summary: A crossing of the central High Atlas that usually starts in the Aït Bouguemez valley and climbs by the Tarkeddit plateau to the long summit ridge of Ighil M'Goun at 4,071 m, descending through the M'Goun gorges. Non-technical, but with several hours above 4,000 m and long days.

name: Jebel Saghro Trek
summary: A walk across the dry volcanic range between the High Atlas and the Sahara, typically from Tagdilt towards Nkob, over Jbel Kouaouch at 2,592 m and passes such as Tizi n'Tazazert. Low enough to stay largely snow-free, so it is walked in the winter months when the High Atlas routes are closed.
